Last updated November 14, 2026.

Illinois property tax is set by county and township assessors, and appeals go first to the county board of review.

What the official sources say

  • Board of review complaint that the assessment is over/under-assessed to affect the current year must be filed within 30 calendar days after the date of publication of the assessment list (Sec. 12-10); mailed complaints are filed as of postmark date; complaints must be in writing; where a change of $100,000+ in assessed valuation is sought, board serves the petition on taxing districts at least 14 days before hearing. (35 ILCS 200/16-55(d), (d-5), (h), (i); source)
  • General Homestead Exemption (35 ILCS 200/15-175): reduction equals the increase in current EAV above 1977 EAV, up to a max of $10,000 in Cook County, $8,000 in counties contiguous to Cook, $6,000 in all other counties (per IDOR PIO-74, R-07/25). (35 ILCS 200/15-175; source)
  • Senior Citizens Homestead Exemption (age 65+): max EAV reduction $8,000 in Cook County and contiguous counties, $5,000 in all other counties; Cook County requires annual application to the Cook County Assessor. (35 ILCS 200/15-170; source)
  • Low-income Senior Citizens Assessment Freeze Homestead Exemption (senior freeze): age 65+, household income limit $75,000 or less for taxable year 2026 (payable 2027), $77,000 for 2027, $79,000 for 2028 and after; freezes EAV at base year; Form PTAX-340 filed annually with Chief County Assessment Office. (35 ILCS 200/15-172; source)
  • Other exemptions: Persons with Disabilities $2,000 EAV reduction (15-168); Standard Homestead Exemption for Veterans with Disabilities $2,500/$5,000/first $250,000 EAV by disability percentage (15-169); Returning Veterans $5,000 (15-167); Homestead Improvement Exemption up to $75,000 fair cash value ($25,000 assessed) for 4 years (15-180). (35 ILCS 200/15-167, 15-168, 15-169, 15-180; source)
  • Senior Citizens Real Estate Tax Deferral Program (320 ILCS 30): age 65+, deferral is a loan secured by lien, repaid when property is sold or transferred, within one year of death, or 90 days after property ceases to qualify; max deferral 80% of taxpayer's equity. (320 ILCS 30; source)
  • Current text: property sold at a tax sale may be redeemed any time before expiration of 3 YEARS from the date of sale (vacant non-farm property, 7+ unit residential, or commercial/industrial property: 1 year). Changes by P.A. 103-555 apply to tax certificates issued on or after 1-1-24; changes by P.A. 104-553 (eff. 7-10-26) apply to certificates issued on/after its effective date. An older ILGA mirror page shows 2.5 years (older version) - 2.5 years should NOT be used for current certificates without verifying certificate issue date. (35 ILCS 200/21-350 (P.A. 103-555; 104-553); source)
  • Tax deeds are exempt from state transfer tax. (35 ILCS 200/31-45(f); source)
  • Collector's scavenger sale: minimum bid $250 or one-half of the tax if total liability is under $500; sale not final until court confirmed; upon confirmation extinguishes in rem lien of general taxes, but does not affect owner's personal liability; certificate owner may petition for tax deed within 6 months before expiration of redemption period under Sections 22-30 to 22-55; unsold properties re-offered annually. (35 ILCS 200/21-260(a), (b), (d), (e); source)

What we could not confirm

  • PTAB filing deadline and exemption amounts not shown above.

Complaints are generally due within 30 days after publication of the assessment list (35 ILCS 200/16-55). Confirm the date with your county.

title: Illinois Quitclaim Deed: Recording, Transfer Tax and When It Works
content:
Illinois Quitclaim Deed: Recording, Transfer Tax and When It Works

Cash Home Buyers in Illinois
Cash Offer in 24 Hours
  • Illinois Quitclaim Deed: inherited, behind on payments, tenants or repairs, we buy the house as-is
  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a Illinois Quitclaim Deed sale
  • Turn the Illinois Quitclaim Deed offer down and you owe us nothing

Selling an Illinois House? Get a Cash Offer

We buy as-is.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

An Illinois deed is recorded with the county recorder of deeds, and transfer tax can apply.

What the official sources say

  • Quitclaim deed may be in substance the statutory form ('convey and quit claim ... all interest'); form should have a 3.5 x 3.5 inch blank space for recorder (failure does not affect validity); conveys grantor's then-existing legal/equitable rights but not after-acquired title unless words added; recording of a quitclaim solely to reflect a legal name change (same grantor/grantee) is exempt from recording fees (P.A. 104-40, eff. 1-1-26). (765 ILCS 5/10; source)
  • Transfer declaration (PTAX-203) must accompany a deed presented for recordation (or be presented within 3 business days of transfer, whichever earlier), signed by at least one seller and one buyer or agents; deed not accepted for recordation without it except as 31-45 provides. (35 ILCS 200/31-25; source)
  • IDOR: PTAX-203 and variants are submitted via MyDec in participating counties; other counties use fill-in forms. (IDOR RETT page; source)
  • State Illinois transfer tax is imposed on the privilege of transferring title to Illinois real estate (also beneficial interests and controlling interests) at 50 cents for each $500 of value or fraction of $500 stated in the declaration; if the transferring document states the transfer is subject to a mortgage, the outstanding mortgage amount is excluded from the tax basis; tax is due whether or not a document is recorded. (35 ILCS 200/31-10; source)
  • Recorder/registrar of titles of the county collects the state tax by selling revenue stamps at 50 cents per $500 or fraction; paper stamps phased out by Dec 31, 2025, after which counties issue electronic revenue stamps or alternative indicia. (35 ILCS 200/31-15(a); source)
  • A deed cannot be accepted for filing by a recorder unless revenue stamps in the required amount have been purchased from the recorder (except exempt deeds under 31-45); stamps are affixed by the recorder before or after recording at grantee's request. (35 ILCS 200/31-20; source)
  • A transfer declaration, signed by at least one seller and one buyer (or their attorneys/agents), must be presented to the recorder with the deed, or within 3 business days after the transfer is effected, whichever is earlier; the form is prescribed by the Department of Revenue; a deed is not accepted for recordation without it (except as provided in 31-45). (35 ILCS 200/31-25; source)

Last updated November 14, 2026.

Illinois charges a state transfer tax of 50 cents per $500, and some counties and cities add their own.

What the official sources say

  • State Illinois transfer tax is imposed on the privilege of transferring title to Illinois real estate (also beneficial interests and controlling interests) at 50 cents for each $500 of value or fraction of $500 stated in the declaration; if the transferring document states the transfer is subject to a mortgage, the outstanding mortgage amount is excluded from the tax basis; tax is due whether or not a document is recorded. (35 ILCS 200/31-10; source)
  • Recorder/registrar of titles of the county collects the state tax by selling revenue stamps at 50 cents per $500 or fraction; paper stamps phased out by Dec 31, 2025, after which counties issue electronic revenue stamps or alternative indicia. (35 ILCS 200/31-15(a); source)
  • A deed cannot be accepted for filing by a recorder unless revenue stamps in the required amount have been purchased from the recorder (except exempt deeds under 31-45); stamps are affixed by the recorder before or after recording at grantee's request. (35 ILCS 200/31-20; source)
  • A transfer declaration, signed by at least one seller and one buyer (or their attorneys/agents), must be presented to the recorder with the deed, or within 3 business days after the transfer is effected, whichever is earlier; the form is prescribed by the Department of Revenue; a deed is not accepted for recordation without it (except as provided in 31-45). (35 ILCS 200/31-25; source)
  • Statutory exemptions from state transfer tax include: deeds to/from governmental bodies and charitable/religious/educational organizations (still must file declaration); deeds securing debt; confirmatory/corrective deeds without added consideration; actual consideration less than $100; tax deeds; deeds releasing security; deeds of partition; deeds in exchange of real estate (money difference taxable); deeds issued to a mortgage holder pursuant to foreclosure or transfer in lieu of foreclosure; certain Home Ownership Made Easy Act purchases (declaration still required). (35 ILCS 200/31-45(a)-(m); source)
  • County board may impose a county transfer tax at 25 cents for each $500 of value or fraction stated in the declaration; collected by recorder before recording; deeds exempt under 35 ILCS 200/31-45 are also exempt; the county tax is in addition to other state/municipal privilege taxes; mortgage outstanding excluded from basis. (55 ILCS 5/5-1031(a); source)
  • IDOR: Form PTAX-203 transfer declaration (and 203-A, 203-B) can be submitted via MyDec; MyDec also accepts City of Chicago Form 7551 Real Property Transfer Tax Declaration and declarations for participating counties; non-MyDec counties use fill-in PDF forms. (IDOR Real Estate Transfer Tax page (references 35 ILCS 200/31-1 to 31-70); source)
  • City of Chicago Dept of Finance: Chicago transfer tax is $3.75 per $500 of transfer price (City portion) plus $1.50 per $500 (CTA portion, for transfers on/after April 1, 2008) = $5.25 per $500; 'In general, The Buyer is responsible for $3.75 and the Seller is responsible for $1.50.'. (Chicago Municipal Code ch. 3-33 (3-33-030); source)
  • Chicago exemptions listed include transfers by court order of a primary residence between members of a legally recognized couple in a legal separation/divorce, transfers to lenders in foreclosure or in lieu, tax deeds, deeds securing debt, transfers under $500; a CTA-portion refund exists for transferees age 65+ who occupy the property one year if price is $250,000 or less (Section 3-33-060(O)). Exemption must be supported by facts/documentation in the declaration. (Chicago Municipal Code 3-33-060; source)

  • Current text: property sold at a tax sale may be redeemed any time before expiration of 3 YEARS from the date of sale (vacant non-farm property, 7+ unit residential, or commercial/industrial property: 1 year). Changes by P.A. 103-555 apply to tax certificates issued on or after 1-1-24; changes by P.A. 104-553 (eff. 7-10-26) apply to certificates issued on/after its effective date. An older ILGA mirror page shows 2.5 years (older version) - 2.5 years should NOT be used for current certificates without verifying certificate issue date. (35 ILCS 200/21-350 (P.A. 103-555; 104-553); source)
  • Tax deeds are exempt from state transfer tax. (35 ILCS 200/31-45(f); source)
  • Collector's scavenger sale: minimum bid $250 or one-half of the tax if total liability is under $500; sale not final until court confirmed; upon confirmation extinguishes in rem lien of general taxes, but does not affect owner's personal liability; certificate owner may petition for tax deed within 6 months before expiration of redemption period under Sections 22-30 to 22-55; unsold properties re-offered annually. (35 ILCS 200/21-260(a), (b), (d), (e); source)
  • Scavenger sale redemption for sales on/after Sept 9, 1993: penalty interest of 3% per month (first 2 months), 12% (2-6 months), 24% (6-12), 36% (12-18), 48% (18-24), then 48% plus 6% per year, on taxes/costs due; non-owner-occupied-single-family redemptions also require payment of other delinquent taxes. (35 ILCS 200/21-260(f); source)

Last updated November 14, 2026.

Illinois foreclosures go through court, and owners have a statutory redemption period.

What the official sources say

  • Redemption period for residential real estate ends on the later of (i) 7 months from the date all mortgagors were served/submitted to jurisdiction or (ii) 3 months from entry of judgment of foreclosure; for non-residential foreclosures it is the later of 6 months from service or 3 months from judgment. (735 ILCS 5/15-1603(b)(1)-(2) (as amended P.A. 104-417, eff. 8-15-25); source)
  • Redemption period is shortened to the later of the end of any reinstatement period or 60 days after judgment if the court finds the value is under 90% of the redemption amount and the mortgagee waives deficiency; shortened to 30 days after judgment if the property is abandoned. (735 ILCS 5/15-1603(b)(3)-(4); source)
  • Owner of redemption must give written notice of intent to redeem to mortgagee's attorney at least 15 days (excluding weekends/court holidays) before the designated redemption date; once expired, the right of redemption is not revived. (735 ILCS 5/15-1603(e), (c)(1); source)
  • Circuit Court of Cook County Chancery Division runs a Mortgage Foreclosure Mediation Program: homeowners who received a court summons get free housing counseling and legal assistance; first step is a free meeting with a housing counselor via toll-free helpline (855) 452-2637; homeowners not yet in foreclosure are referred to Cook County Legal Aid for Housing and Debt (855) 956-5763. (Circuit Court of Cook County, Chancery Division Mediation page (no statute cited); source)

Illinois evictions go through the Eviction Act and the courts.

What the official sources say

  • Landlord may demand rent and notify tenant in writing that unless paid within a stated time, not less than 5 days after service, the lease will be terminated; if unpaid, landlord may commence eviction without further notice. Notice must prominently state the partial-payment language specified in the statute. (735 ILCS 5/9-209; source)
  • Holdover tenancy week-to-week: 7 days' written notice; any term under one year (other than week-to-week): 30 days' written notice (subject to Section 9-207.5). (735 ILCS 5/9-207; source)
  • Chicago Tenant Opportunity to Purchase Act (TOPA) pilot (Woodlawn / 606 district; enforcement began March 1, 2025; pilot expires Dec 31, 2029): owner must give tenants and Dept of Housing a Notice of Intent to Sell at least 60 days before listing for properties with 5+ rental units, or 30 days before listing for 1-4 units; tenants have right of first refusal; deposit capped at 5% of price; exemptions include family transfers, foreclosure/deed in lieu, bankruptcy, tax sale. Applies only to the pilot district, not all of Chicago. (Chicago Municipal Code ch. 5-11 (5-11-050, 5-11-060); source)
